teams.synopsis: A new #1 — four elite pieces, and Conklin quietly might be the difference-maker at TE.
teams.blurb: We got a new top team after 3 weeks of play. Duce's team takes the jump into the number-1 spot after Baylen and Deniz's losses last week. Headlined by King Henry and Waddle, this team doesn't look like a top team on paper, but there are 4 players on this team that are elite at their respective positions three weeks into the season (Wentz, Henry, Waddle, and Conklin). Conklin was a nice pickup for this team at the TE position, but we'll look to see if this success can continue in Week 4 and Duce can remain undefeated.

teams.synopsis: From 14th to a top-5 team in two weeks — Lamar's MVP-level run is carrying the way.
teams.blurb: Remember when he was ranked 14th? Yeah, that was only 2 weeks ago, but look at Malich now. His team has been going off the past few weeks, and I wouldn't be surprised if they do it again. <mark class="hl-player">Lamar</mark> has been playing at an MVP level, <mark class="hl-player">Jamaal Williams</mark> is the sneaky RB8, and <mark class="hl-player">Devonta Smith</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Chris Olave</mark> are some of the best young WRs in the league (both are top 24). Despite <mark class="hl-player">Swift</mark> being sidelined, this team should be considered a top-5 team for the foreseeable future.

teams.synopsis: A misleading 1-2 record hides the 3rd-most points scored in the league.
teams.blurb: He might be 1-2, but Bileydi's team is packed with top players this fantasy season. There were some trade rumors of this team acquiring a true RB1 in <mark class="hl-player">Joe Mixon</mark>, but even though they fell through, this team will be doing just fine. Deniz has seen a fair share of bad luck this season, having the 3rd-most PF but also an above-average PA — which gives him a misleading 1-2 record. My advice to Bileydi would be to trade one of his WRs, since you can only play 3 but he has 4 great options. He could trade one of these players plus other assets to land a low-mid-tier RB1, because we don't know how <mark class="hl-player">Gibson</mark> will look once the rookie <mark class="hl-player">Brian Robinson</mark> returns in the upcoming weeks.

teams.synopsis: A rough week cost the top spot, but Saquon's dominance keeps this team in the mix.
teams.blurb: Losing the number-1 spot must not feel good for Baylen, but I'm guessing he could've seen this coming. I thought Baylen was going to have a solid week last week, but his team severely underperformed, and in return we dropped him down the rankings. Now, I think this team can redeem itself this week, but if they underperform again, this team should begin to worry a little and maybe look for some trades to bring in a new culture. <mark class="hl-player">Saquon</mark> has undoubtedly been the best RB in football so far, though, so never count out a team with an elite player like that.

teams.synopsis: A win doesn't move the needle here — Ekeler needs to show more before this team climbs.
teams.blurb: Even though he won last week, I can't find a reason to raise this team up any spots. A very good team on paper, but I need to see more out of <mark class="hl-player">Ekeler</mark> to put this team any higher. There have also been trade rumors surrounding this team about potentially looking for a flex option — because even though <mark class="hl-player">Dillon</mark> is a mid-low-tier RB2, he's looking to upgrade to a WR. I'm confident in this team's chances in Week 4, but it will be difficult to beat the top team in the league.

teams.synopsis: A lucky matchup masks a quiet week — this roster is still just one piece from the top.
teams.blurb: A mediocre showing from Brandon earned him his 2nd win, and even though his WRs didn't put up 80 points combined, he found a way to win. This team definitely got lucky by playing the bottom team this week, and I wouldn't be surprised if he loses this 6th spot next week. That being said, Brandon does have a talented roster and is only a piece away from being a top team in the PFFL — look for him to potentially trade for a QB, or maybe even an upgrade at TE.

teams.synopsis: The Njoku pickup fixed the one weak spot — the ceiling just got a lot higher.
teams.blurb: I like this spot a lot for Andrew because of how good this team has been playing recently, but there are still some questions surrounding this team in the long run. With the addition of Njoku at TE, Root has finally gotten rid of his weakest position and raised his team's ceiling much higher. He's projected for 120.3 points in Week 4 at the moment, so look for this team to climb the ranks if all goes well.

teams.synopsis: Winning without Mike Evans and defying every expectation — don't judge this book by its cover.
teams.blurb: I really don't like this team, but respect — I swear this team should not be doing as well as it is, but then again, Gorman has been wrong about a lot of things. Gorman's bench is depleted, but I guess that doesn't matter at all, because his lineup won without <mark class="hl-player">Mike Evans</mark> last week. This is the definition of don't judge a book by its cover, and I'm lowkey excited to see how it performs in the upcoming weeks. I'm rooting for them, and I think they have what it takes to be a middle-of-the-pack team — I'd be shocked if they finish as a playoff team.

teams.synopsis: The best of the middle tier — matchup luck, not talent, is what's holding the champ back.
teams.blurb: The rest of the teams on this list are all similar in talent and can be grouped together as a tier below everyone else — the best of this group being Ben. This team has been falling ever since Week 1, but I think Ben's team has been a little unlucky when it comes to matchups. He has the 3rd-highest PA, so it's been difficult for Ben to get wins even when his team scores at the league average. This team will improve once <mark class="hl-player">Fournette</mark> gets in the end zone, and maybe <mark class="hl-player">Godwin</mark> can be a solid WR2 when he returns from injury, because <mark class="hl-player">Claypool</mark> isn't cutting it. Will the defending champ rise back up the ranks this week?

teams.synopsis: Average across the board for now, but a CMC monster week could change the story fast.
teams.blurb: A little bit of a fall for this manager, but I think he'll get right back on track this week. Despite Ryan calling for this team to trade everyone, I still think this team has the talent to be an above-average squad. That being said, this team is very average in multiple categories, so I don't know where he goes from here. Also, keep an eye out for <mark class="hl-player">CMC</mark> to have a monster week and re-solidify himself as the RB1.

teams.synopsis: Winless but not outmatched — the toughest schedule in the league, not a lack of talent.
teams.blurb: Might be weird that an 0-3 team moved up the rankings this week, but this team has a solid squad that can compete with anyone. They have the highest PA in the league, but also more PF than the league average — on paper, this squad should have at least one win, but they've had very formidable opponents through the first three weeks. They don't have much potential to do great things in Week 4, so I'm expecting another loss for Aidan, sadly.

teams.synopsis: Winless but climbing anyway — Kupp is carrying this roster almost single-handedly.
teams.blurb: The other 0-3 team follows — listen, I know you might think it's impossible to jump up the rankings after losing, but Geg did it. This team is really being carried by <mark class="hl-player">Kupp</mark>, but I think it has the potential to be solid. <mark class="hl-player">Pierce</mark> is beginning to look like a low-end RB2, and <mark class="hl-player">Aiyuk</mark> could be a flex option with <mark class="hl-player">Jimmy G</mark>. I really don't know if this team will win in Week 4, but I won't be shocked if they get their first win either.

teams.synopsis: A 2-1 record masking the 2nd-fewest points in the league — the trades still haven't come.
teams.blurb: I was really debating putting this team last, but I couldn't do it. They're 2-1 somehow, and Cole's team is just a little worse on paper. The RB duo in this organization is projected for less than 20 combined, and Cooks only catches a third of his targets. It's extremely strange for Anthony's team to have the 2nd-fewest PF in the PFFL, but it's happening. I still think more trades need to be done for this team to look anything better than a bottom-5 team, but then again, I've been wrong about previous teams.

teams.synopsis: Three good players and not much else — the worst PFAA in the league says it all.
teams.blurb: Sorry, brother, I'm gonna keep it short and simple. Your team has 3 good players and the rest are nobodies. I think it's time you trade <mark class="hl-player">Brown</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Jefferson</mark>, or <mark class="hl-player">Javonte</mark> for some good pieces to fill out your roster, because <mark class="hl-player">Penny</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">Knox</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Moore</mark> have proved that you can't start them on a weekly basis. Cole has the worst PFAA in the league, and I am calling it now: this team will put up bottom-5 numbers this week. Javonte might go off for 25 points, though.
